questions.q: Complete: (a) 50 N opposes a 10 kg body moving at 10 m/s; deceleration = ______. (b) Time to stop = ______.
(a) Two bodies stick together after collision — elastic or inelastic? (b) Name the energy stored in a stretched spring.

(a) Which law forbids the conversion of 100% heat into work? (b) With which form of energy is heat most closely associated?

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: A ball of mass m is thrown up with speed v and returns to the thrower with the same speed. Find the change in its momentum.
questions.answer:
Initial momentum = mv upward; final = mv downward.
Taking up as positive: Δp = (−mv) − (mv) = −2mv, i.e. 2mv downward. The magnitude of momentum is unchanged.

or.q: Identify the action–reaction forces on a book lying on a table.
or.answer: The book pushes down on the table with a force equal to its weight (action); the table pushes up on the book with an equal force (reaction). They act on different bodies.

questions.q: A particle moving with kinetic energy 3.6 J hits a spring of force constant 180 N/m. Find the maximum compression.
questions.answer:
All the KE becomes spring energy: ½kx² = 3.6.
x² = 2 × 3.6/180 = 0.04 ⇒ x = 0.2 m.

or.q: A 50 kg body is placed on the smaller piston (0.1 m²) of a hydraulic lift whose bigger piston is 10 m². Find the weight it can lift. (g = 10 m/s²)

questions.q: A Carnot engine between an unknown temperature and the ice point has an efficiency of 75%. Find the unknown temperature.
An open pipe of length l₁ and a closed pipe of length l₂ resonate with the same fork in their fundamental modes. Find l₁/l₂.
questions.answer:
Open: ν = v/2l₁. Closed: ν = v/4l₂.
v/2l₁ = v/4l₂ ⇒ l₁ = 2l₂ ⇒ l₁/l₂ = 2.

questions.q: The electric flux through a Gaussian surface is zero. Does it mean that (a) the charge enclosed is zero and (b) the field is zero everywhere on the surface?
questions.answer:
(a) Yes — by Gauss's theorem φ = q/ε₀, so the net charge enclosed is zero.
(b) Not necessarily — field lines may enter and leave, giving zero net flux even where E ≠ 0 (e.g. a surface near an outside charge).

questions.q: Write the expression for the energy stored in a capacitor in three forms.
questions.answer: U = ½CV² = Q²/2C = ½QV. It is stored in the electric field between the plates.

questions.q: What is meant by the unidirectional (rectifying) property of a p-n junction? Give one application.
questions.answer: It conducts easily in forward bias but hardly at all in reverse bias, so current flows in one direction only. Application: a rectifier converting ac to dc.

questions.q: Draw the symbol and truth table of a NOT gate.
questions.answer: Symbol: a triangle with a small circle at the output. Truth table: A = 0 → Y = 1; A = 1 → Y = 0 (Y = Ā).

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Verify Stokes' law (F = 6πηrv) by dimensional analysis.
questions.answer:
Let F = k ηᵃ rᵇ vᶜ.
[MLT⁻²] = [ML⁻¹T⁻¹]ᵃ[L]ᵇ[LT⁻¹]ᶜ.
M: a = 1. T: −a − c = −2 ⇒ c = 1. L: −a + b + c = 1 ⇒ b = 1.
So F = kηrv, with k = 6π found by experiment.

or.q: Obtain the terminal velocity of a sphere of radius r and density ρ falling through a fluid of viscosity η and density σ.
or.answer:
At terminal velocity, weight = upthrust + viscous drag:
(4/3)πr³ρg = (4/3)πr³σg + 6πηrv.
v = 2r²(ρ − σ)g/9η.

questions.q: What are electric field lines? State three properties. Draw them for a single positive charge and for a dipole.
questions.answer:
Field lines are imaginary curves whose tangent at any point gives the direction of the field there.
Properties: (1) they start on positive and end on negative charges; (2) two lines never cross; (3) they are dense where the field is strong; (4) they meet a conductor's surface at right angles.
Positive charge: straight lines pointing radially outward. Dipole: lines curve from +q round to −q.

questions.q: Explain the principle, construction and working of a moving-coil galvanometer.
questions.answer:
Principle: a current-carrying coil in a magnetic field feels a torque.
Construction: a rectangular coil on a soft-iron core between concave poles (radial field), suspended by a phosphor-bronze strip or springs, with a pointer and scale.
Working: the deflecting torque NBIA is balanced by the restoring torque kθ, so I = (k/NBA)θ ∝ θ. The scale is linear.

or.q: Explain the principle and working of a cyclotron.
or.answer:
Principle: a charge moving perpendicular to B moves in a circle, with period T = 2πm/qB independent of speed.
Two hollow dees between magnet poles have an alternating voltage of frequency f = qB/2πm across the gap. Ions accelerate across the gap each half-cycle and move in larger semicircles inside the dees, gaining energy each time until they emerge at high speed.

questions.q: Write three distinguishing features of fringe patterns in Young's double-slit experiment and in single-slit diffraction.
questions.answer:
(1) In YDSE all fringes are of equal width; in diffraction the central maximum is twice as wide as the rest.
(2) In YDSE bright fringes are equally bright; in diffraction their intensity falls rapidly away from the centre.
(3) YDSE uses light from two coherent sources; diffraction uses wavelets from different parts of a single wavefront.

or.q: In single-slit diffraction, how does the angular width of the central maximum change when (i) the slit is narrowed, (ii) the screen is moved farther and (iii) light of shorter wavelength is used?
or.answer:
Angular width = 2λ/a.
(i) a decreases ⇒ angular width increases.
(ii) Unchanged — the angle does not depend on D (the linear width increases).
(iii) λ decreases ⇒ angular width decreases.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Derive the capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor and show how a dielectric changes it. How do the charge, p.d., field and energy change when a dielectric slab is inserted (a) with the battery connected and (b) after disconnecting the battery?
questions.answer:
Plates of area A, separation d, charge ±Q: σ = Q/A, E = σ/ε₀, V = Ed = Qd/ε₀A, so C = Q/V = ε₀A/d. With a dielectric filling the gap, E is reduced K times, so C = Kε₀A/d.
(a) Battery connected (V fixed): C → KC; Q → KQ; E = V/d unchanged; U = ½CV² → KU.
(b) Battery disconnected (Q fixed): C → KC; V → V/K; E → E/K; U = Q²/2C → U/K.

questions.q: A metal rod of length l rotates with frequency ν about one end, which is at the centre of a circular metal ring, the other end touching the ring. A uniform field B is parallel to the axis. Obtain the emf between the centre and the ring.
questions.answer:
Take an element dr at distance r; its speed is v = ωr. The emf across it is de = Bv dr = Bωr dr.
e = ∫₀ˡ Bωr dr = ½Bωl².
With ω = 2πν: e = πνBl².
